subject: SIG/ISO evidence kickoff: control mapping and walkthrough for Evercrest Financial
messages:
From: Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@evercrest.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Trevor Lane <trevor.lane@evercrest.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG/ISO request: control mapping & evidence for procurement

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for taking our RFP. Our procurement and compliance teams are trying to finalize the security appendix this quarter. Attached is a condensed SIG-lite we use for buy-side validation; we need a control mapping and evidence packet for the sections marked "control verification required".

Top asks:
- Mapping from SIG control IDs to Redwood control owners and evidence artifacts (where possible).
- A representative evidence packet for encryption/key management, privileged access, and change control.
- High-level network segmentation diagram and enclave descriptions for customer workload isolation.
- SOC 2 report (most recent) and ISO 27001 scope statement if available.

Can we schedule a 60-minute technical walkthrough next week to go through the mapping and call out any gaps? Prefer Tue/Wed mornings PT.

Thanks,
Maya Thompson
Manager, Vendor Risk & Procurement
Evercrest Financial

Attachment: evercrest-sig-lite-compact.pdf (pdf)
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@evercrest.com>
Cc: Trevor Lane <trevor.lane@evercrest.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG/ISO request: control mapping & evidence for procurement

Hi Maya — appreciate the clear ask and the SIG-lite. We're happy to support.

Quick summary of what we can deliver by your timeline:
1) Control mapping spreadsheet that links SIG control IDs to Redwood control IDs, control owner, and available artifacts (deliverable: evidence-index-evercrest.xlsx).
2) Representative evidence packet containing: SOC 2 report (redacted where needed), KMS key rotation logs sample, privileged access review export, change control runbook excerpt, and network segmentation diagram.
3) A follow-up 60-minute technical walkthrough to validate the mapping and surface any gaps.

Proposed slots: Tue 6/6 09:00-10:00 PT or Wed 6/7 10:30-11:30 PT. Please confirm preferred slot and any additional names to include.

Internal note: Mina, can you pull the latest KMS rotation sample, privileged access roster export, and a local copy of the SOC 2 PDF for redaction? Jonas — please surface the network segmentation diagram for the private tenant design. I will assemble the initial evidence-index and push to the shared Drive link below.

Thanks — I aim to have the initial evidence bundle to you 6/5 EOD PT.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: (none)
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Action: artifacts for Evercrest SIG mapping

Mina — quick asks to support the Evercrest packet:
- KMS key rotation logs (redacted IDs ok) for last 6 months — CSV sample fine (file: kms-key-rotation-log-sample.csv)
- Privileged access review export (latest quarterly) with role mapping, remove PII
- Change-control runbook excerpt (policy + one change ticket screenshot)
- Network segmentation diagram for dedicated/tenant isolation (high-res PNG)

Can you drop these in the Evidence folder on Drive by EOD Monday (6/5)? If any item will take longer, flag here and I'll manage expectations with Evercrest.

Thanks — Priyom

Priyom — sending what I could pull as a starting set. Notes inline.

Attached (uploaded to Drive and also included here):
- redwood-soc2-report-2027.pdf (redacted) — contains scope and auditor statement.
- kms-key-rotation-log-sample.csv — 6 months, key IDs pseudonymized.
- privileged-access-export-q1-2028.csv — roles + last access review date; removed usernames.
- network-segmentation-diagram.png — shows dedicated tenant VLANs and control plane separation.
- change-control-excerpt.pdf — policy excerpt and one ticket screenshot (ticket id masked).

Caveats: the privileged access export omits individual usernames for data protection; team leads are listed by role. If Evercrest needs raw usernames for a live review we need a signed NDA amendment — let me know and I'll start the proc steps.

I also created an initial mapping tab in evidence-index-evercrest.xlsx with control owners and where each artifact maps. Jonas, please verify the network enclave labels; I used the private-tenant and shared-control-plane names from infra.

Mina
Security & Trust, Redwood Inference

Thanks Priyom and Mina — this is great and exactly the level of detail we need to start our internal assessment.

We'll lock the walkthrough for Tue 6/6 09:00-10:00 PT. I'll send a calendar invite and our third-party ISV assessor (name: Trevor Lane) will join. Two quick clarifications before the call:
1) For privileged access we typically need a sample audit trail for a small set of users (redacted) to validate process. If an NDA amendment is required, please propose text and we'll expedite.
2) For the SOC 2 PDF: can you confirm the report covers production regions in us-west-2 and eu-central-1? Our scope requires region coverage.

If both items are OK, we'll proceed to a draft contract redline and schedule final attestation once the walkthrough confirms the mapping.

Best,
Maya Thompson
Manager, Vendor Risk & Procurement
Evercrest Financial
